summary:
Every visitor to West Virginia stands first under the federal travel-document regime. Since January 2025, Executive Order 14168 has required United States identity documents to reflect sex assigned at birth, the State Department stopped processing the X marker, and new passports are issued only as M or F from the supporting documents submitted. A trans or nonbinary visitor can therefore arrive holding papers that do not match their presentation, with airport screening and visa decisions following the same national rules, including the February 2025 State Department policy refusing visas to trans athletes seeking entry to compete in women's sporting events.

West Virginia's own restriction is statutory and recently enacted. Governor Patrick Morrisey signed Senate Bill 456, the 'Riley Gaines Act', on 12 March 2025, after the state Senate passed it on 3 March and the House of Delegates on 6 March. The law defines 'woman' as an adult human of the female sex and 'man' as an adult human of the male sex, and frames its purpose as preserving women's single-sex spaces on that biological basis.

The facilities covered reach considerably further than restrooms. The statute names locker rooms, bathrooms, rape crisis centers, dormitories, prisons and domestic-violence shelters, which places a trans visitor inside its scope in university accommodation, correctional settings and victim-support services as well as in washrooms and changing areas. At the signing the governor stated that bathrooms, locker rooms, domestic violence shelters and rape crisis centers should be kept private for women only, an official statement of intent that shapes how the provisions are likely to be applied.

A national legal risk assessment dated July 2026 places West Virginia in its 'Worst States' group, a tier covering fifteen states and one step below the four states designated do-not-travel: Florida, Idaho, Kansas and Texas. The same assessment records Idaho as the most recently promoted do-not-travel state, the fourth so designated, following a felony bathroom ban carrying up to five years imprisonment that is partially blocked by courts but remains in force wherever no gender-neutral option exists. The assessment's national frame is one of worst policies in effect, with the 2026 legislative season continuing to degrade trans rights alongside the federal measures.
tangentialFactors:
Facility restrictions of the West Virginia type are not isolated. Bathroom bans applying to trans people in K-12 schools and some government buildings are in force across nine states and one territory, with some jurisdictions treating trans facility use as a criminal offence in certain circumstances, while twenty-nine states, four territories and the District of Columbia impose no such ban. Enforcement has moved past statute text: in April 2025 a trans student who announced he was there to break the law used a women's restroom at the Florida state capitol and was arrested and handcuffed, which civil-rights attorneys identified as the first known arrest under a state bathroom-restriction law.

The Movement Advancement Project maintains an equality-map catalogue of state bans on transgender people's use of public bathrooms and facilities according to gender identity, which is the enumeration source for the state-by-state counts above, and a separate identity-document map setting out which jurisdictions permit gender-marker changes on licences and birth certificates and under what conditions. Because those document rules differ state by state, the papers a trans visitor carries were issued under one state's regime and may be tested against another's.

Comparison states show how fast the floor is moving. Kansas has enacted a statute invalidating birth certificates and driver's licences that do not bear sex assigned at birth and barring trans residents from changing those markers, described by rights groups as a template other legislatures are following. Idaho's felony bathroom ban produced its do-not-travel designation in the same period, which situates West Virginia's 'Worst States' grade within a national pattern rather than as an outlier on its own.
localsOnly:
The definitions in Senate Bill 456 bind state institutions that West Virginia residents use every day, not only transient visitors: locker rooms and bathrooms in public buildings, higher-education dormitories, prisons and jails, domestic-violence shelters and rape crisis centers are all named in the statute. A resident of West Virginia has no carve-out from those provisions, and the governor's signing statement puts the intended application beyond doubt.

Residents carry the same federal document constraint as visitors. Birth certificates and driver's licences are state-issued, but passports and other federal identity documents issued since January 2025 reflect sex assigned at birth, so a resident's in-state records and federal records can diverge from each other.

The July 2026 legal risk assessment grades West Virginia among its 'Worst States', one tier below the do-not-travel designation applied to four other states, which is a resident-facing assessment of the laws in force rather than a travel advisory alone.
outOfScopeNotes:
The Movement Advancement Project facility-ban page cited for the state-by-state enumeration returned a 404 response, the project having moved the page. Whether the enumeration has since been revised at a new address is unresolved here.

No source in the inventory states whether West Virginia permits or bars changes to the gender marker on a state driver's licence or birth certificate. That question for residents and visitors is unresolved.

No source records arrests, prosecutions, complaints or civil actions brought under Senate Bill 456 since it took effect in March 2025. Enforcement in practice is unresolved.

The inventory carries nothing on hate-crime protection covering anti-trans motives in West Virginia, nor on recognition of marriages or partners of trans people in the state. Both are unresolved.

The 'Worst States' grade comes from a single published assessment (Erin In The Morning, via Stonewall News, 27 August 2026). Its tier definitions, scoring method and the underlying statutes it weighs are not independently corroborated in this record.
